question: Why is causal masking used when training the Transformer decoder?
expected_answer: It blocks attention to future positions so the model cannot see future outputs during training.
evidence_quote: The self-attention operations in the Transformer’s decoder use a “causal” masking pattern. When producing the ith entry of the output sequence, causal masking prevents the model from attending to the jth entry of the input sequence for j >i. This is used during training so that the model can’t “see into the future” as it produces its output.
evidence_verified: Exact normalized PDF text; AI-assisted source reading. Questions and split fixed before the first PDF retrieval run.
